title: Pinhole Projection Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Computer Vision for Robotics
description: Move a point in front of a pinhole camera and watch the pixel where it lands. Then use the pinhole formula in six problems: five ask for a pixel coordinate, and one runs the formula backward from a pixel and a depth to a distance. Used in Chapter 14.

educational.topic: The pinhole camera model and camera intrinsics
learningObjectives: Calculate the pixel position of a point, or the sideways distance of a point from its pixel and depth, using the pinhole camera model with fx = fy = 500 and the principal point (320, 240), for six problems, to within the tolerance shown, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Move a point and watch its pixel, then apply the projection formula to new numbers with an immediate check
keyQuestions: What happens to the pixel offset from the centre when the depth doubles?
Why is depth needed to turn a pixel back into a position?
commonMisconceptions: A point twice as far away has twice the pixel offset
The pixel (0, 0) is the middle of the picture
Pixels and metres are the same scale everywhere
assessmentOpportunities: Six typed answers, one attempt each; 5 of 6 for mastery
